keyTakeaways: Halloween in India is an urban night out: 2025 listings show hotel dinners, club nights and a beach party across Mumbai, Goa, Delhi and Bengaluru, but no survey counts who takes part.
31 October is not a Halloween holiday anywhere in India; the RBI's October 2026 list closes banks that day only in Ahmedabad, for Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday.
Diwali's Lakshmi Puja falls on 8 November 2026 and 29 October 2027, and in 2027 Bhai Dooj lands on Halloween itself, 31 October (Drik Panchang, New Delhi).
India's own nights for the dead sit close by: Pitru Paksha runs 26 September to 10 October 2026, and Bengal cooks 14 leafy vegetables on Bhoot Chaturdashi before Kali Puja.
On SubhSandesh, festival and wedding pages together are only 3.7% of 3,894 pages measured, and no Halloween usage data exists yet.

faqs.question: Is Halloween celebrated in India?
faqs.answer: Yes, mainly in cities, as costume parties, hotel dinners and club nights on 31 October evening and the nearest weekend. It is not a traditional Indian festival, and no survey has measured how many people join in.

faqs.question: Is it Halloween in India on the same day as in America?
faqs.answer: Yes, the date is 31 October everywhere. IST sits 9.5 hours in front of New York time on that date in 2026 and 2027, so Indian parties start well before American ones.

faqs.question: Do offices and schools close for Halloween in India?
faqs.answer: No. The RBI's October 2026 holiday list closes banks on 31 October only in Ahmedabad, and that is for Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday, not Halloween.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in India in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: It is on 31 October in both years, which falls on the weekend each time (Saturday in 2026, Sunday in 2027). That lets venues hold their main night on Halloween itself.

faqs.question: Does Halloween clash with Diwali?
faqs.answer: Not in 2026, when Lakshmi Puja falls on Sunday 8 November, eight days later. In 2027 the two sit close: Lakshmi Puja is on 29 October and Bhai Dooj lands on 31 October itself.

faqs.question: What is Bhoot Chaturdashi?
faqs.answer: It is Bengal's ghost night, the Chaturdashi just before Kali Puja, when households prepare 14 leafy vegetables known as chauddo shaak. It is the closest Indian parallel to a night of spirits, though it is a home ritual rather than a costume party.

faqs.question: Is there an Indian festival like Halloween?
faqs.answer: Not a direct match. Pitru Paksha, from 26 September to 10 October in 2026, honours ancestors with food offerings, and Bhoot Chaturdashi marks a night of spirits in Bengal; both are solemn or domestic.

faqs.question: Is it wrong for Indians to celebrate Halloween?
faqs.answer: That is a values call, not a fact. Research on South Asian youth finds many join in for fun while treating it as cultural rather than religious, while critics see Westernization; keeping it light and away from family rites avoids most friction.

faqs.question: Is trick-or-treating common among Indian children?
faqs.answer: No Indian survey measures it, and none of the 2025 events we verified was a street trick-or-treat. Treat any claim about how common it is with caution.

faqs.question: Which Indian cities have the most Halloween events?
faqs.answer: Nobody counts them. One October 2025 guide listed events in Mumbai, Goa, Delhi and Bengaluru, ranging from hotel dinners to a beach party at Morjim.

faqs.question: How can I wish someone in India a happy Halloween?
faqs.answer: A message works, and so does SubhSandesh's Halloween card: a private link that runs on any phone or computer, set to partner, best-friend, relative or child mode. Its text is English only, so pick something else for a reader who prefers Hindi or Bengali.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween in India: Who Celebrates It and Where It Meets Diwali

Yes, Halloween is celebrated in India, but as an urban night out rather than a festival: hotel dinners, club nights and costume parties in cities such as Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi and Goa. No holiday list we checked closes for it, and no survey has counted how many Indians take part.

What we can measure is how Indians use SubhSandesh, an India-built greeting platform. Festival and wedding pages together are just 3.7% of 3,894 pages, and from Raksha Bandhan 2026, a separate occasion measured on only 89 pages, nearly half (49.4%) came on Raksha Bandhan itself. SubhSandesh has not yet recorded any Halloween usage, so no figure here counts Halloween pages.

What follows: the holiday status, checked against the RBI holiday list; why Halloween caught on; how it sits next to Diwali in 2026 and 2027; and India's own nights for spirits and ancestors, from Pitru Paksha to Bengal's Bhoot Chaturdashi. City notes use only dated 2025 event listings.

## Is 31 October a holiday anywhere in India?

No. The Reserve Bank of India's [holiday matrix for October 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/HolidayMatrixDisplay.aspx) marks 31 October as a bank holiday in only one city, Ahmedabad, and the reason is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday, not Halloween. Every other bank, office and school runs to its normal calendar.

The weekday helps, because Halloween lands on the weekend both years (Saturday in 2026, Sunday in 2027), so parties need no midweek excuse. Compare Mahalaya Amavasya, the ancestors' new moon on 10 October 2026, which the same RBI list closes banks for in Bengaluru and Kolkata.

## Why has Halloween caught on in Indian cities?

No Indian study measures Halloween directly, so the answer comes from neighbouring research. Anthropologist Ritty Lukose, in a [2005 Journal of Social History paper](https://repository.upenn.edu/bitstreams/412a8191-ed1b-41f3-94e4-ea57aff6743f/download), traces how India's liberalisation from the early 1990s, cutting tariffs and opening state industries to private firms, turned consumption into a new way of being Indian. In her Kerala fieldwork, youth fashion, films and beauty pageants became the place where arguments about Westernization, tradition and modernity were fought.

Halloween fits that pattern. A [2025 study of Halloween on Instagram](https://journals.umt.edu.pk/index.php/JITC/article/download/7326/3359) by Waheed, Ahmad and Bhatti interviewed 16 people in Lahore and found Instagram frames Halloween as a secular, visually appealing lifestyle trend. Young users joined in for entertainment and belonging, and many reframed it as cultural rather than religious.

Pakistan is not India, but the mechanism is the one Indian venues sell to: a festival arriving through phones rather than family tradition. In October 2025 [Harper's Bazaar India](https://www.harpersbazaar.in/travel-food/story/spooky-plans-here-are-the-top-things-to-do-this-halloween-weekend-1296876-2025-10-30) listed Halloween nights across Mumbai, Goa, Bengaluru and Delhi. Claims that international schools or streaming services drove the trend are plausible but unmeasured; we found no Indian data either way.

## Halloween and Diwali dates for 2026 and 2027

Halloween never leaves 31 October, while Diwali moves with the lunar calendar, so the gap between them changes every year. These dates come from [Drik Panchang's Diwali calendar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/diwali/diwali-puja-calendar.html?year=2026) for New Delhi:

- **2026:** Halloween on Saturday 31 October; Dhanteras on Friday 6 November; Narak Chaturdashi, Kali Puja and Lakshmi Puja on Sunday 8 November; Bhai Dooj on Wednesday 11 November.
- **2027:** Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October; Narak Chaturdashi and Kali Puja on Thursday 28 October; Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October; Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October, the same day as Halloween.

In 2026, Halloween arrives eight days before Diwali, while homes are mid-clean. In 2027 it falls two days after Lakshmi Puja and on Bhai Dooj itself, so most families will treat 31 October 2027 as a sibling day first. The Kolkata calendar gives the same Kali Puja dates for both years.

## India's own nights for spirits and ancestors

India's calendar already holds several nights for the dead, and two fall within a month of 31 October. Neither involves costumes or trick-or-treating, which is exactly why the comparison helps.

### Pitru Paksha: 26 September to 10 October 2026

Drik Panchang's 2026 shraddha calendar runs Pitru Paksha from Purnima Shraddha on 26 September to Sarva Pitru Amavasya on 10 October. It describes the period as 15 lunar days when Hindus pay homage to their ancestors, especially through food offerings. The tone is domestic and solemn, centred on named family members rather than a public crowd.

### Bhoot Chaturdashi: Bengal's ghost night

In Bengal, the Chaturdashi just before Kali Puja's new moon is Bhoot Chaturdashi, literally the "ghost fourteenth". A 2020 [ICAR Indian Horticulture article](https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/105370/41249) on indigenous leafy vegetables records the tradition of preparing 14 leafy vegetables, chauddo shaak, on that night.

Drik Panchang lists Narak Chaturdashi and Kali Puja on the same date, 8 November 2026, and on 28 October in 2027. Check a Bengali panjika for which evening your family keeps as Bhoot Chaturdashi.

### How they compare with Halloween

The table sets the four observances nearest to 31 October against Halloween. All dates are for 2026.

| Indian observance | Date (2026) | What it marks | How it compares to Halloween |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pitru Paksha | 26 Sep to 10 Oct | 15 lunar days of food offerings to ancestors | Same theme of the dead, but private and solemn; ends 21 days before 31 Oct |
| Mahalaya (Sarva Pitru Amavasya) | 10 Oct | Last day of Pitru Paksha | Bank holiday in 2 cities (Bengaluru, Kolkata); Halloween gets 0 |
| Bhoot Chaturdashi | Eve of Kali Puja, 8 Nov listed | Bengal's ghost night; 14 leafy vegetables cooked | Closest in spirit, but a home ritual; 8 days after Halloween |
| Kali Puja and Lakshmi Puja | 8 Nov | Diwali's main night | Lamps and puja against costumes and parties; 8 days later |

India's ancestor observances cluster in the weeks either side of Halloween. They are household rites, while Halloween in India is almost entirely a ticketed night out.

## Is Halloween a Western import? The sensitivity debate

Yes; the real argument is whether that matters. Lukose's 2005 work shows the same shape in Kerala: new global habits among the young become a stage for older debates about Westernization and tradition, and those debates centre on young women far more than on young men.

The Lahore study maps positions you will also hear at an Indian family table. Parents and educators stressed cultural preservation, religious scholars warned against Westernization, and young people joined in for fun while calling it cultural, not religious.

If you are hosting, the middle path is simple. Keep it a costume night, never a parody of anyone's rites, and do not schedule it over a relative's shraddha or a Bhai Dooj lunch.

## Halloween in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi and Goa

Every listing below comes from Harper's Bazaar India's guide of 30 October 2025, so it is a 2025 snapshot, not a 2026 schedule. Check each venue's own page before you dress up.

- **Mumbai:** a Hogwarts-themed wizarding dinner at Sesame, Hyatt Centric Juhu (31 October 2025), and a drag, music and art night at Pioneer Hall, Bandra.
- **Goa:** Hellcultured at Uncultured, the speakeasy inside The Unseen Hotel, Assagao (31 October and 1 November 2025), and Soundcraft's season-opening party on Morjim Beach.
- **Delhi:** evenings at Grappa, Shangri-La Eros New Delhi (31 October and 1 November 2025), and at Cosy Box, One Golden Mile.
- **Bengaluru:** The Hebbal Café at Courtyard by Marriott Hebbal, Quattro at The Leela Bhartiya City (7 pm to 11 pm on 31 October 2025), and a Sunburn Union night on 1 November 2025.

The spread says something on its own. Goa's entries were a speakeasy and a beach party, while two of Bengaluru's three were hotel meals; that is a reading of one guide, not a measured trend.

### Staying safe at a Halloween party

We will not quote party-safety statistics, because we found none specific to Halloween in India. These points come from common sense, not a dataset:

- Book your ride home before you leave, especially in 2026, when the night is a Saturday and a late finish meets weekend traffic.
- Patch-test face paint and fake blood on your inner arm a day ahead.
- Take masks off when walking on roads, and add one light-coloured piece to a dark costume.
- At housing-society events, label each child's costume with a parent's phone number.

## Sending a Halloween greeting from India

SubhSandesh is built in India, and its [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) greets a single person; it is no way to invite guests. You fill in a name, a short letter, a maximum of six pictures and one word for the pumpkin.

On their screen, a tiny haunted house opens after three knocks, your word lights up inside a carved pumpkin, the letter appears under a torch beam in the attic; then a closing question invites them to become your boo. You can pick a partner, bestie, relative or child mode, and the Kids setting stays sweet-spooky, without blood or sudden frights.

At the end they receive a Boo License image at Instagram Story dimensions (1080×1920), and their first reply lands in your inbox as an email. Expect a phone screen: phones carry 48.3% of all views our shared pages get, measured platform-wide and not for Halloween in particular. The cinematic option is the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium), adding a recorded voice message (60 seconds maximum), a dozen photos and a time lock that keeps it sealed until a moment you pick.

### When to send something other than a pumpkin

Sometimes the festival on the other side of the week matters more. In these cases, skip the pumpkin:

- A grandparent who sees Halloween as a Western import will value a Diwali call far more.
- On 31 October 2027, Bhai Dooj takes the day; send your sibling something for that instead.
- All text on the card is English, and a relative more at home in Hindi or Bengali may get lost.
- One recipient per card means no housing-society invites and no party tickets.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The five ranking pages are 2013-2014 wire copy, a 2023 listicle, a Twinkl stub and spam, so this is the only page that checks the RBI holiday list, gives Diwali-relative dates for 2026 and 2027 (including Bhai Dooj on 31 October 2027), sources Bhoot Chaturdashi and cites peer-reviewed research on Halloween's spread in South Asia; that is a genuine reason for an answer engine to prefer it.
